info.name: LOS - Rule Engine & Loan Eligibility API
info.description:
Rule Engine (dropdowns from Lookup Master) and Loan Eligibility.

Run order: 0. Authentication -> 1. One-time lookup setup (once per bank) -> 2. Rule Engine 2-7 -> 3. Loan Eligibility.

Variables: baseUrl, bankCode (e.g. ABC001), today (yyyy-MM-dd).

item.name: 1. One-time setup: Rule Engine lookups
item.description:
The Rule Engine screen's dropdowns come from Lookup Master. Run this folder once per bank (logged in), or create the same lookups on the Lookup Management screen.

- Rule Parameter (Check)
- Rule Operator (When value is)
- Rule Decision (Then)
- Firm Registration (options of the Firm Registration choice parameter)

Codes 10020-10023 are examples; any free codes work. The backend finds the lookups by name (configurable: app.rule-engine.lookups.parameter / operator / decision) and understands each value by its name (Below / Above / Between / Is, Allow / Override / Reject, FOIR / DTI / LTV / CIBIL).

item.name: 2. Rule Engine
item.description:
Rule = Check (param) + When value is (op) + value (a, and b for Between) + Then (decision) [+ Add to rate % (offset) for Override] + effective date.
param / op / decision accept the lookup sub code (from GET /options), the lookup name or its id. The screen's short operator codes lt / gt / between / eq work too.
Rules apply from their effective date (default today); no approval. Two active rules of the same parameter may not overlap (400). Between includes both ends; 'Above 50' means more than 50.
Responses carry the screen's list fields (param, op, a, b, decision, offset, active, effectiveDate) plus full lookup details and a readable description.

item.name: 3. Loan Eligibility
item.description:
POST /api/loan-eligibility/assess takes the Loan Eligibility screen's fields and checks them against the active rules.

Net income = income - expenses. FOIR = (existing debt + EMI) / net income. DTI = (existing debt + EMI) / income. LTV = loan / security value (only with a security value). CIBIL as entered.

- No Reject / Refer -> Eligible (requested amount).
- Refer rule, or only FOIR / DTI / LTV rejected and a lower amount passes -> Refer for Review with eligibleAmount = highest amount that passes (rounded down to Rs 1,000).
- Otherwise Not Eligible, eligibleAmount 0.
Override rules add their offset: finalInterestRate = annualInterestRate + rateOffset; eligibleEmi uses it.
ratios[] gives the Status column (Within limit / Rate +x% / Outside limit / Not applicable / No rule). Rules on custom parameters (Age, Firm Registration ...) use additionalFacts.

Requires login.

header.description: Bank code (e.g. ABC001) or bank database name

exec: console.log(json.data.decision + " | eligible " + json.data.eligibleAmount + " @ " + json.data.finalInterestRate + "% | " + JSON.stringify(json.data.ratios) + " | " + JSON.stringify(json.data.reasons));
